label: S-A4 two defensible answers (option c, a 41% speed increase, also doubles Ek)

item.question_text: A trolley is rolling along a level floor. Which change would double the energy in its kinetic energy store?

options.d: Doubling both its mass and its speed

feedback.a: Doubling the speed multiplies the kinetic energy by 4, because it depends on speed squared.
feedback.c: Kinetic energy depends on speed squared, so a small increase in speed cannot double it.
feedback.d: Doubling both multiplies the kinetic energy by 2 × 4 = 8.

misconception_map.c: slip: underestimates the effect of a speed increase
misconception_map.d: slip: thinks the two changes add rather than multiply

item.explanation: Kinetic energy is proportional to mass, so doubling the mass doubles it.

label: S-A1 'movement energy ... used up' in the explanation (terminology and conservation error)

item.question_text: A school bus of mass 8000 kg is travelling at \(10\,\text{m/s}\). Calculate the energy in its kinetic energy store.

wrong.misconception: This leaves out the half. Kinetic energy is \(\tfrac{1}{2} \times 8000 \times 10^{2} = 400\,000\,\text{J}\).

item.explanation: \(E_k = \tfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} = \tfrac{1}{2} \times 8000 \times 10^{2} = 400\,000\,\text{J}\). When the bus brakes to a stop, this movement energy is used up by the brakes.

label: S-B1 assesses momentum (HT Forces), not kinetic energy

item.question_text: A ball of mass 2 kg moves at 3 m/s. Which of its quantities has the value 6 kg m/s?

feedback.b: Kinetic energy is measured in joules: here it is \(\tfrac{1}{2} \times 2 \times 3^{2} = 9\,\text{J}\).
feedback.c: Weight is a force, measured in newtons.
feedback.d: The speed squared is 9, in m²/s².

misconception_map.c: slip: confused mass times speed with weight
misconception_map.d: slip: squared the speed without a reason

item.explanation: Mass × velocity = 2 × 3 = 6 kg m/s: that is momentum.
